name: Lunar age
seoDesc: Lunar age: work out your Chinese lunar age (2) from your current age. A free everyday life calculator with the formula, units and a worked example.
summary: The Lunar age calculator returns your Chinese lunar age (2) from the 3 fields on the form. No sign-up, no page reload, and the relationship behind it is printed below. It suits a practical question that turns up in daily life. The unit chips sit next to the boxes, which is where most hand-calculation mistakes start.

sections.title: How does the Lunar age calculator work?
sections.html:
The Lunar age calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports your Chinese lunar age (2) in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case (the calculate using); then you type in your current age.

Press Calculate and the page works through the equation with the values you supplied and derives the rest; it then keeps up with you as you correct a typo.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: What do you need to enter?
sections.html:
• Pick the option that matches your case — 2 options, such as chinese calendar and hijri calendar. The choice changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier, so it is worth reading the options carefully.
  • A single on/off switch — tick it for “Chinese New Year has occurred”, leave it clear for the other case. It changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier.
  • A plain number with no unit attached.

2 fields on this form are a choice rather than a number. Those choices decide which version of the calculation applies, so they are worth setting before you worry about the digits.

sections.title: The formula behind the Lunar age calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Your Chinese lunar age=your current age + 2
Your Chinese lunar age=your current age + 1
Hijri lunar age=(1027 ÷ 1000) × your current age

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: What is a worked example?
sections.html:
Suppose Calculate using set to Chinese calendar and Your current age = 10. Working through the relationship above gives Your Chinese lunar age = 11 and Hijri lunar age = 10.

Read it as a template. Every number above can be replaced with one of yours; only the relationship between them is fixed.

  1. Enter the values listed above, matching the units each box asks for.
  2. Read off the result. Any field you leave empty is the one the calculator solves for.
  3. Sanity-check the number against the relationship: Your Chinese lunar age = 11 and Hijri lunar age = 10 should be roughly the size you expected from Calculate using set to Chinese calendar and Your current age = 10.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Lunar age calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Turning a rough idea into a number you can act on
  • Checking a figure someone else quoted
  • Testing how sensitive an answer is to one input
  • Any time the same 1 figures keep coming back — your current age — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.
  • Compare two scenarios by changing the input that actually differs between them, and keep the rest fixed, so the difference you see is the difference you meant to test.
  • If a result surprises you, look at the order of magnitude before the digits: a plausible number in the wrong unit looks more convincing than an implausible one, and is easier to miss.
  • Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.

sections.title: What are the limits worth knowing?
sections.html:
Every tool draws a boundary somewhere. For the Lunar age calculator, these are the ones that matter:

  • The 2 drop-downs on this page offer a fixed list of cases. A value that is not on the list cannot be entered, and the nearest option is not always a good substitute.
  • The calculator reports what the relationship implies; it does not judge whether the inputs themselves are sensible, so a figure that is out by a factor of ten will produce an answer that is out by the same factor.

faq.q: What does the Lunar age calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns your Chinese lunar age (2), derived from your current age. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Lunar age calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for your current age, which is 3 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There are several choices to make (2 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

With the values the page starts from, the calculator reports Your Chinese lunar age = 11. Treat that as a reference point rather than a recommendation: it exists so you can tell at a glance whether your own inputs are on the same scale.

faq.q: Is the Lunar age calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.
